title: cost-optimization-defaults-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce autotuned defaults for batching and KV caching, add quantization profile presets, and UI tooling for unit-economics recommendations. No breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost and operational overhead by shipping a set of sensible defaults and UX tooling that recommends batching, caching and quantization profiles per-route/workload. This PR implements autotuneable defaults, a small library of quantization profiles, and a unit-economics panel used by the Console and CLI. Changes are conservative: defaults can be overridden per-route and rollout happens behind a feature flag. Summary of changes: 1) autotune: implement heuristic autotuner that picks batch size and KV cache TTL based on latency SLOs and traffic distribution; 2) defaults: new config schema with batch/cache default entries and safe fallback logic; 3) quant profiles: three vetted quantization profiles (fp16, int8-dynamic, int8-aggressive) with metadata and compatibility matrix; 4) unit economics tooling: backend endpoint and frontend panel that surface estimated $/1000 tokens and projected savings for suggested profiles; 5) tests & telemetry: added integration tests for autotune decisions and dashboards for regression alerts. Migration & rollout: feature-flagged rollout to 10% of traffic for two weeks, metrics tracked: tokens-per-second, p95 latency, and cost-per-token. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-3421) [x] unit + integration tests [x] end-to-end perf run in perf-canary [x] console UI and CLI exposure [x] docs update. Impact: expected average token cost reduction of 12%-28% for tail-heavy workloads in perf runs while keeping p95 latency within SLOs. Backwards compatibility: config defaults are opt-in via feature flag; existing routes unchanged unless admin enables autotune. See commits and files changed below for details.

Ethan Zhou: Concern about int8-aggressive profile stability on older GPUs. Reply: added compatibility matrix and guardrails that fallback to int8-dynamic or fp16 based on kernel availability. Also added perf-canary job to validate across fleets.
